validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch shows credentialId-based lookup at lines 147-149 with fallback to 'primary'. This is intentional design - matching by credentialId is correct. Legacy rows without credentialId falling back to primary is acceptable behavior, not a bug.

validated_findings.body: The optional chaining makes the push a no-op, so co-host destination calendars are discarded and no host calendar events are created — the exact scenario this PR aims to fix.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Silently missing calendar entries for collective hosts.
validated_findings.impact: The optional chaining makes the push a no-op, so co-host destination calendars are discarded and no host calendar events are created — the exact scenario this PR aims to fix.
validated_findings.root_cause: `destinationCalendar` is typed/initialized as possibly `null` while team calendars are appended with optional chaining instead of initializing the array.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Initialize the array before pushing, e.g. `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars];`.
validated_findings.title: Collective team destination calendars silently dropped when organizer has none
validated_findings.trigger: A COLLECTIVE team event where neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (so `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`), but co-hosts have their own destination calendars.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 1078 verbatim: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. When destinationCalendar is null (lines 1063-1067 show it can be null), optional chaining makes push a no-op, silently dropping team calendars.

validated_findings.failure_mode: Booking references persisted without credential linkage.
validated_findings.impact: The created `_video` booking reference is stored with `credentialId: undefined` (previously `result.credentialId`), so later cancellation/reschedule cannot resolve the specific video credential for that reference.
validated_findings.root_cause: Rewriting the ternary replaced the non-calendar branch value `result.credentialId` with `undefined`.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Keep the video branch's credential: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : result.credentialId` or simply `credentialId: result.credentialId ?? undefined`.
validated_findings.title: Video booking references lose credentialId in EventManager.create
validated_findings.trigger: Any booking with a dedicated video location (e.g. Zoom, Google Meet) — the video result is not a calendar result.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 170 verbatim: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. For video results (!isCalendarType), credentialId is now always undefined. Previously it was `result.credentialId` for video results.

validated_findings.body: `updateEvent` never returns `externalId` or `credentialId`, so the regenerated references drop the calendar id and credential id that were previously taken from `evt.destinationCalendar`, breaking subsequent updates/deletes on that calendar.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Booking references written with undefined calendar/credential identifiers.
validated_findings.impact: `updateEvent` never returns `externalId` or `credentialId`, so the regenerated references drop the calendar id and credential id that were previously taken from `evt.destinationCalendar`, breaking subsequent updates/deletes on that calendar.
validated_findings.root_cause: Reference fields were switched to result properties that the update code path does not populate.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Populate these from the event's destination calendar (or make `updateEvent` return `externalId`/`credentialId`) instead of reading fields the result never sets.
validated_findings.title: updateLocation references now always store undefined externalCalendarId/credentialId
validated_findings.trigger: Editing a booking location, which routes calendar results through `updateAllCalendarEvents` → `CalendarManager.updateEvent`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 208-209 show `externalCalendarId: result.externalId, credentialId: result.credentialId ?? undefined`. CalendarManager.updateEvent (lines 313-322) returns EventResult without externalId/credentialId fields, so these will be undefined.

validated_findings.body: `createEvent` is called without `externalId`, so `result.externalId` is undefined and the new booking reference stores no `externalCalendarId` (previously taken from `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`), causing later updates/deletes to fall back to the primary calendar.
validated_findings.impact: `createEvent` is called without `externalId`, so `result.externalId` is undefined and the new booking reference stores no `externalCalendarId` (previously taken from `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`), causing later updates/deletes to fall back to the primary calendar.
validated_findings.root_cause: The refactor only forwards `externalId` in the credentialId branch, dropping it in the integration-type fallback.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Pass `destination.externalId` in this branch: `createEvent(c, event, destination.externalId)`.
validated_findings.title: createAllCalendarEvents omits externalId for destinations without credentialId
validated_findings.trigger: A destination calendar row whose `credentialId` is null (legacy data), which takes the integration-type fallback branch.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 380 shows `createEvent(c, event)` called without externalId parameter in the else branch (no credentialId). Line 370 shows the credentialId branch passes `destination.externalId`. Missing externalId means booking reference lacks externalCalendarId.

validated_findings.impact: The string literals compile fine but no longer track the enum, so an enum change silently makes team-event detection (and the `=== "COLLECTIVE"` checks added later in the same file) wrong instead of failing at compile time.

validated_findings.suggested_fix: Restore enum comparisons: `eventType.schedulingType === SchedulingType.COLLECTIVE || eventType.schedulingType === SchedulingType.ROUND_ROBIN`.

validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a stylistic concern about using string literals vs enum. The code is functionally correct - the strings match the enum values. Loss of compile-time safety is a code quality issue, not a bug.

validated_findings.body: The published interface contract now demands an argument that only one implementation honors; single-argument call sites fail to compile (`Expected 2 arguments, but got 1`), and third-party calendar apps built against the previous signature break on upgrade.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Compile-time breakage / contract mismatch for callers and implementers of the `Calendar` interface.
validated_findings.impact: The published interface contract now demands an argument that only one implementation honors; single-argument call sites fail to compile (`Expected 2 arguments, but got 1`), and third-party calendar apps built against the previous signature break on upgrade.
validated_findings.root_cause: A new parameter was appended to a widely implemented public interface method as required rather than optional.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Declare the new parameter as optional, e.g. `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId?: number): Promise<NewCalendarEventType>;`, so existing callers and implementations remain source-compatible while Google Calendar can still read it.
validated_findings.title: Calendar.createEvent makes credentialId a required parameter, breaking existing single-argument callers/implementers
validated_findings.trigger: Any consumer of the exported `Calendar` interface that invokes `calendar.createEvent(event)` with a single argument (out-of-tree/app-store code, tests, or future call sites) is type-checked against the new two-parameter signature; only `GoogleCalendarService` (`createEvent(calEventRaw, credentialId)`) actually consumes the second argument, all other 12 CalendarService implementations declare `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 221 shows `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)` with required second param. Repository search shows 12 other CalendarService implementations declare `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` with single param, breaking interface contract.

validated_findings.body: External webhook/API consumers receive an array where they previously received an object, so property access yields `undefined` (or throws in strict consumers) and destination-calendar-dependent integrations silently stop working, with no deprecation or versioning note.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Downstream integrations break at runtime because the serialized payload shape changed without a migration path.
validated_findings.impact: External webhook/API consumers receive an array where they previously received an object, so property access yields `undefined` (or throws in strict consumers) and destination-calendar-dependent integrations silently stop working, with no deprecation or versioning note.
validated_findings.root_cause: The shape of a field that is part of the externally observable webhook/API payload was changed in place from object to array.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Either keep the singular field and add a new plural field (e.g. `destinationCalendars?: DestinationCalendar[]`), or explicitly document/version this payload-shape breaking change in the webhook/API docs shipped with the PR.
validated_findings.title: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar changed from a single object to an array without a compatibility path for payload consumers
validated_findings.trigger: CalendarEvent instances are serialized into outbound webhook payloads and API responses (see `apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts` expectations changing from `destinationCalendar: null` to `destinationCalendar: []`); an existing subscriber reads `payload.destinationCalendar.externalId` after this deploy.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: While the type change from object to array is real (line 171), this is an intentional API change for the PR's purpose. The webhook test was updated. External consumers are not proven to exist or be affected without documentation.

validated_findings.body: Consumers that only check one empty form (e.g. `?? []` versus a `null` check) behave differently for equivalent "no destination calendar" states, making destructuring such as `const [main] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yield `undefined` in some paths and not others.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Inconsistent null/empty handling across producers and consumers of CalendarEvent.
validated_findings.impact: Consumers that only check one empty form (e.g. `?? []` versus a `null` check) behave differently for equivalent "no destination calendar" states, making destructuring such as `const [main] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yield `undefined` in some paths and not others.
validated_findings.root_cause: The array conversion kept the legacy `| null` union in addition to optionality, creating redundant empty encodings.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Narrow the declaration to a single empty representation, e.g. `destinationCalendar?: DestinationCalendar[];`, and normalize producers to emit `[]` (or omit the field) instead of `null`.
validated_findings.title: destinationCalendar type permits three distinct empty states (undefined, null, []), producing inconsistent call-site handling
validated_findings.trigger: Producers of CalendarEvent already diverge under the new type: `handleNewBooking.ts` sets `destinationCalendar: ... : null` when no calendar exists, while `handleCancelBooking.ts` sets `[]`; every consumer must therefore guard for `undefined`, `null` and empty array (`event.destinationCalendar && event.destinationCalendar.length > 0`).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The three empty states (undefined, null, []) is a type design concern but not a concrete bug. The code handles these cases with checks like `evt.destinationCalendar && evt.destinationCalendar.length > 0`.

validated_findings.body: Events constructed through `CalendarEventBuilder`/`CalendarEventClass` can never carry `schedulingType`, so consumers relying on it (collective-host destination-calendar logic) see it as `undefined` for builder-produced events, diverging from `handleNewBooking`-produced events.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Builder-produced CalendarEvents silently lack the new field, causing behavioral divergence between event construction paths.
validated_findings.impact: Events constructed through `CalendarEventBuilder`/`CalendarEventClass` can never carry `schedulingType`, so consumers relying on it (collective-host destination-calendar logic) see it as `undefined` for builder-produced events, diverging from `handleNewBooking`-produced events.
validated_findings.root_cause: Interface extended without the paired builder update mandated by the in-file convention comment.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add `schedulingType?: SchedulingType | null;` to `packages/core/builders/CalendarEvent/class.ts` and a corresponding `setSchedulingType` in `builder.ts`, as the interface comment requires.
validated_findings.title: New schedulingType field on CalendarEvent not mirrored in the CalendarEvent builder classes required by the interface's own comment
validated_findings.trigger: The comment immediately above this interface states "If modifying this interface, probably should update builders/calendarEvent files"; `packages/core/builders/CalendarEvent/class.ts` was updated for `destinationCalendar` (line 26) but declares no `schedulingType` member, and `builder.ts` exposes no setter for it.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim about CalendarEventBuilder not having schedulingType is speculative. The interface comment is advisory. Without evidence that builder-produced events cause actual failures, this is ungrounded.
